chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Furat, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, raising it, said:

Five men who had committed adultery were brought to Umar, so he ordered that the Hadd penalty be established upon each one of them. The Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was present, so he said: 'O Umar, this is not their judgement.' He said: 'So you establish the judgement upon them.' He brought forward one of them, so he struck his neck; and he brought the second, so he stoned him; and he brought the third, so he whipped him the Hadd; and he brought the fourth, so he whipped him half the Hadd; and he brought the fifth, so he reprimanded him.

So Umar was confounded and the people were astounded by his action. Umar said: 'O Abu al-Hasan, five people in one case, you established five different Hadd penalties upon them, not one resembling the other!' The Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the first, he was a Zimmi who had exited his covenant, so there was no judgement for him except the sword. As for the second, he was a married man, so his Hadd was stoning. As for the third, he was not married, so he was whipped the Hadd. As for the fourth, he was a slave, so we whipped him half the Hadd. And as for the fifth, he was an insane man whose intellect was overpowered.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali differentiate the punishments for five men accused of adultery?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the nuanced application of *Hadd al-Zina* by Imam Ali (AS), distinguishing between *Muhsan* (married/free), *Ghayr Muhsan* (unmarried/free), *Zimmi* (non-Muslim subject), *Abd* (slave), and *Majnun* (insane). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that legal penalties are contingent upon the specific attributes (*ahwal*) of the accused, a concept often contrasted with the more generalized application seen in Sunni traditions. The incident serves as a practical demonstration of *ijtihad* and the importance of contextualizing divine law to individual circumstances.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Muhammad Bin Al Furaat, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata, raising it, said,

‘They came to Umar with five people who had committed adultery. So he ordered that the Penalty (Hadd) be established upon each one of them, and Amir Al-Momineenasws was present. So heasws said: ‘O Umar! This is not (supposed to be) their judgement’. So he said, ‘So youasws establish the judgement upon them’. So they brought forward one of them, so heasws struck his neck; and they brought the second one, so heasws stoned him; and they brought the third one, so heasws whipped him the Penalty (Hadd); and they brought the fourth, so heasws whipped him half the Penalty (Hadd); and they brought the fifth, so heasws reprimanded him’.

So Umar was confounded and the people were astounded from hisasws actions. So Umar said, ‘O Abu Al-Hassanasws, five people in one judgement, five judgements being established upon them, not a thing from it resembling the other!’ So Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘As for the first one, he was a Zimmi (under the responsibility) who had exited from the responsibility (of the government), there was no judgement for him except for the sword. And as for the second one, so he was a married man, his Penalty (Hadd) was the stoning. And as for the third one, so he was not married, was whipped the Penalty (Hadd). And as for the fourth one, so he was a slave, we whipped him half the Penalty (Hadd); and as for the fifth, so he was an insane, his intellect had been overcome’.
